answer: Each agent must post a bond locked until its claimed work is independently checked; a randomly selected auditor compares the result with the task’s public requirements and can slash the bond for fabricated or duplicate identities. Auditors stake too, so approving a sham risks their own funds. A sybil can multiply accounts, but each one needs fresh capital and exposes it to loss, making attacks costly even when identities are cheap. In a canyon economy, a gale of fake agents cannot turn an oasis of rewards into profit without risking more than it can steal.
